html:
The Funj Sultanate, also called the Sultanate of Sennar, was a Muslim kingdom on the Blue Nile in what is now Sudan, from 1504 to 1821.

It followed the Christian Nubian kingdoms of Makuria and Alwa. Its first sultan, Amara Dunqas, founded the capital Sennar on the Blue Nile in 1504. The Funj were a people of unclear origin who ruled over Nubians, Beja, Arab tribes and others. At its height, in the late 1600s, the sultanate stretched from the Third Cataract of the Nile south to the edge of the Ethiopian highlands, and west to Kordofan.

The sultans invited Sufi holy men from Egypt and Arabia. Their schools spread Islam and Arabic, which helped form the Arab tribes of modern Sudan. Sennar traded gold, ivory and enslaved people north to Egypt and east to the Red Sea, and fought both Ethiopia and Darfur.

In 1762 the Hamaj, a group of regents, seized real power, and the state broke into civil wars. In 1821 the army of Muhammad Ali of Egypt marched up the Nile, and the last sultan surrendered.
sum: The Funj Sultanate, also called the Sultanate of Sennar, was a Muslim kingdom on the Blue Nile in what is now Sudan, from 1504 to 1821.
